test_strategy.rationale: Equivalence partitioning applies because the input condition divides into discrete partitions (temperature change requested vs. not requested). State-based testing applies because the system moves through distinct process states (transitioning to activated process state upon trigger). Use case testing applies because the requirement defines a multi-step scenario where a trigger (temperature change request) initiates a workflow that activates a process and yields a downstream request.

test_cases.title: Verify activation of determine heating/cooling mode process on valid temperature change request
test_cases.preconditions: The climate control system is operational and waiting for user or automated inputs.
steps: Issue a request to change the target temperature from 20°C to 22°C.
Monitor the system process activation logs and output request queue.
test_cases.expected_result: The 'determine heating/cooling mode' process is activated and successfully generates a heating/cooling request.

test_cases.title: State transition from Idle/Inactive to Active process state upon receiving a temperature change request
test_cases.preconditions: The 'determine heating/cooling mode' process is in the Inactive/Idle state.
steps: Trigger a temperature change request in the system.
Verify the state of the 'determine heating/cooling mode' process.
Verify the resulting output of the process state transition.
test_cases.expected_result: The process transitions from Inactive/Idle to Active state and outputs a heating/cooling request.

test_cases.title: User-initiated temperature change workflow generating downstream mode request
test_cases.preconditions: User is authenticated and viewing the thermostat control interface.
steps: User inputs a new temperature setpoint via the interface.
System receives and registers the temperature change request.
System activates the 'determine heating/cooling mode' process.
Process evaluates setpoint versus current ambient temperature and emits a heating/cooling request.
test_cases.expected_result: The workflow completes end-to-end: temperature change request activates the process, which successfully dispatches a heating/cooling request.
